paper_metadata.title: Plastic slip mechanisms in high-temperature titanium alloys: Insights into silicide and Ti3Al precipitates on ductility

High-angle annular dark-field imaging (HAADF) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) reveal Zr and Si enrichment in these precipitates ( Fig. 1 b), with an average particle size of 0.22 μ m.

Aging at 700 ◦ C for 5 h reveals nano-sized α 2 particles. TEM bright-field images show sparse silicides, while SAED patterns and TEM dark-field images highlight abundant nano- α 2 precipitates, whose average size is approximately 4.85 nm ( Fig.2 f – h).
The microstructure of Ti-74 alloy after IMDF is illustrated in Fig. 2 . The matrix mainly consists of nearly equiaxed α with residual β phase ( Fig. 2 a).
The microstructure of Ti-74 alloy after IMDF is illustrated in Fig. 2 . The matrix mainly consists of nearly equiaxed α with residual β phase ( Fig. 2 a).
TEM-BF images reveal several S 2 -type silicides ( Fig. 2 b), though their volume fraction is lower due to the reduced Zr content, which has little effect on the silicide size.
The dispersed nanoscale silicides at grain boundaries reduce the prevalence of basal slips and enhance pyramidal 〈 c + a 〉 as the primary slip mechanism ( Fig. 5 a).
Conversely, α 2 nanoparticles promote basal 〈 a 〉 slip, resulting in planar dislocations and reduced ductility.
These nano- α 2 precipitates can induce planar slip at room temperature ( Fig. 5 b).
The increased participation of non-basal slip systems alleviates localized stress and reduces the likelihood of premature fracture, thereby enhancing ductility [ 54 ].
Conversely, Ti-74 alloy exhibits dominant basal slip with suppressed prismatic and pyramidal slip, characterized by an average SF value below 0.4 ( Fig. 4 d – f), leading to reduced ductility.

The interaction between mobile dislocation and α 2 precipitates obstructs dislocation movement and hinders cross slip. Concurrently, dislocation accumulation within the α matrix in Ti-74 forms dislocation walls, promoting localized deformation and microcrack initiation, leading to premature fracture [ 55 ].
